prompt: Each moment starts a buying process. Sort it by where the trigger comes from.

cards.text: Halfway through a long run, Amir feels thirsty and wants a sports drink.
cards.explanation: The trigger comes from inside Amir, so it is an internal stimulus.

cards.text: Nora walks past a bakery window and sees fresh croissants.
cards.explanation: The trigger comes from the world around her, so it is an external stimulus.

cards.text: After weeks of back pain, Ben decides his mattress has to go.
cards.explanation: The discomfort comes from Ben himself, so it is an internal stimulus.

cards.text: A coworker's new noise-cancelling headphones make Ines want a pair.
cards.explanation: Seeing someone else's product is an outside trigger, so it is an external stimulus.

cards.text: A radio ad reminds Paul that his car needs new tires.
cards.explanation: The ad is outside Paul, so it is an external stimulus.

cards.text: Late at night, Mia's stomach growls and she orders a pizza.
cards.explanation: Hunger comes from inside Mia, so it is an internal stimulus.

prompt: Sam is buying a stroller and gathers information from four places. Match each source type to what Sam uses.

pairs.match: Two friends who already own a stroller
pairs.explanation: Friends and family are personal sources, and they tend to be the most effective.

pairs.match: The brand's own website and a store salesperson
pairs.explanation: Advertising, websites and salespeople come from the company selling the product.
Mass media and rating organizations are public sources.

pairs.match: Pushing the display model around the store
pairs.explanation: Handling and trying the product yourself is experiential.

question_text: Right after paying for an expensive laptop, Karim keeps wondering if he should have bought the other brand. What is he experiencing?
hint: The purchase is already made. Think about the stage that comes after it.

options.option_text: Need recognition, triggered by an internal stimulus.
options.option_explanation: Need recognition starts the buying process. Karim has already bought the laptop, so he is past that stage.

options.option_text: Evaluation of alternatives within his choice set.
options.option_explanation: Evaluating alternatives happens before the purchase decision. Karim's doubts come after he has bought.
Correct. Cognitive dissonance, or buyer discomfort caused by postpurchase conflict, is a common occurrence.

options.option_text: Situational factors blocking his purchase decision.
options.option_explanation: Situational factors come between intention and decision. Karim did make the purchase, and his discomfort came afterwards.

prompt: Perception is the process by which people select, organize, and interpret information. Which part of perception is each shopper doing?

cases.text: Walking through a busy mall, Lina notices only the shoe ads and tunes out everything else.
cases.explanation: Lina picks out a few pieces of information and ignores the rest, so she is selecting.

cases.text: In the cereal aisle, Omar mentally sorts the boxes into healthy brands and sugary brands.
cases.explanation: Omar arranges what he sees into groups, so he is organizing.

cases.text: Julie sees the highest price on the wine list and decides it must be the best wine.
cases.explanation: Julie gives the price a meaning, so she is interpreting.

cases.text: Scrolling past dozens of posts, Theo stops only at the one showing the headphones he has been wanting.
cases.explanation: Theo lets one post through and skips the others, so he is selecting.

cases.text: Before buying a tent, Aisha lines up the reviews she has read into pros in one column and cons in another.
cases.explanation: Aisha puts the information into a structure, so she is organizing.

cases.text: Marc sees a plain, recycled-paper package and concludes the brand cares about the environment.
cases.explanation: Marc reads a meaning into the package, so he is interpreting.

question_text: A maker of aluminum cans sees its orders drop after people start buying fewer soft drinks. Which idea explains this?
hint: Where does the can maker's demand ultimately come from?

options.option_text: Elastic demand, since can buyers react strongly to price.
options.option_explanation: Nothing about price changed here. B2B demand is also more inelastic than B2C demand, not more elastic.

options.option_text: Postpurchase dissonance among soft drink buyers.
options.option_explanation: Dissonance is discomfort after a purchase. The drop here comes from consumers buying fewer drinks in the first place.

options.option_text: Market structure, since can makers serve many small buyers.
options.option_explanation: A business marketer normally deals with far fewer but far larger buyers, and buyer count does not explain this drop.

options.option_text: Derived demand, which comes from consumer demand.
options.option_explanation: Correct. Business demand is derived demand; it ultimately derives from the demand for consumer goods, here soft drinks.

prompt: A hospital is buying new patient monitors. Match each buying-center role to the person who plays it.

pairs.match: The nurses who will work with the monitors every shift
pairs.explanation: Users are the people who will actually use the product.

pairs.match: The biomedical engineer whose test report shapes the shortlist
pairs.explanation: Influencers affect the decision without making it.

pairs.match: The purchasing agent who negotiates terms and places the order
pairs.explanation: Buyers have formal authority to select suppliers and arrange the purchase.

pairs.match: The hospital director who approves the supplier
pairs.explanation: Deciders have the power to make the final choice.

pairs.match: The assistant who controls which sales reps get a meeting with the director
pairs.explanation: Gatekeepers control the flow of information to the others.
